rmt-2016-adv-01.prompt: List all triples of positive integers $\{p_1,p_2,p_3\}$ where $p_1,p_2$, and $p_3$ are all prime, $p_1<p_2<p_3$, and $p_1,p_2$ differ by $2$, $p_2,p_3$ differ by $2$. For example $\{6,8,10\}$ is a triple that satisfies the last two properties, but not the first one, so it is not included in the answer.

rmt-2016-adv-02.prompt: An ant is walking on the edges of an icosahedron of side length $1$. Compute the length of the longest path that he can take if he never crosses the same edge twice, but is allowed to revisit vertices.

rmt-2016-adv-03.prompt: Compute the number of trailing zeros of $2016!$.

rmt-2016-adv-05.prompt:
Let $d(n)$ be the number of positive integer divisors of a positive integer $n$. For example, $d(6)=4$, because the divisors of $6$ are $1,2,3$, and $6$. Compute
$$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{d(n)}{n^2},$$
given that $\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac1{n^2}=\frac{\pi^2}6$.

rmt-2016-adv-06.prompt: Suppose $n>0$ is an integer which, when written in base $10$, has all digits either $0$ or $1$. If $17$ evenly divides $n$, find the smallest possible value of $n$.

rmt-2016-adv-07.prompt: Lennart and Eddy are playing a betting game. Lennart starts with $7$ dollars and Eddy starts with $3$ dollars. Each round, both Lennart and Eddy bet an amount equal to the amount of the player with the least money. For example, on the first round, both players will bet $3$ dollars. A fair coin is then tossed. If it lands heads, Lennart wins all the money bet; if it lands tails, Eddy wins all the money bet. They continue playing this game until someone has no money. What is the probability that Eddy ends with $10$ dollars?

rmt-2016-adv-08.prompt: Consider a $2011\times2012$ grid of points from $(1,1)$ to $(2011,2012)$ with the point $(1066,1453)$ removed. Starting at $(1,1)$ and only moving up or to the right at each step, compute the number of different ways you can get to $(2011,2012)$. You may express your answer using multiple binomial coefficients.

rmt-2016-adv-10.prompt: A continuous real-valued function $f$ on the positive real numbers has the property that for all positive $x$ and $y$, $f(xy)=xf(y)+yf(x)$. Determine all such functions $f$.
rmt-2016-adv-10.answer: $f(x)=c\,x\ln x$ for an arbitrary real constant $c$
